assessment: The article makes unusually testable bearish calls: later equity lows and a Q1 policy-rate peak both failed. The recession call also failed. Gold and tobacco later performed well, while BMY disappointed, illustrating why sector narratives cannot substitute for per-asset evidence. Custody and reserve-proof analysis was stronger than the inferred regulatory consensus or the claim that a chain halt destroys proof-of-stake history.
